title: TeenHQ MakerSpace Studio
registrationEvidence: Registration is full; check the organizer page for current waitlist options.
description: Up to 5 teens at a time can use the space to utilize our 3D printers, Poster Printer, GlowForge, Sewing & Serger Machines, Cricut, Button Press, and miscellaneous craft supplies.
parentSummary: Up to 5 teens at a time can use the space to utilize our 3D printers, Poster Printer, GlowForge, Sewing & Serger Machines, Cricut, Button Press, and miscellaneous craft supplies.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Middle and high schoolers: Come explore the TeenHQ MakerSpace! Up to 5 teens at a time can use the space to utilize our 3D printers, Poster Printer, GlowForge, Sewing & Serger Machines, Cricut, Button Press, and miscellaneous craft supplies. Work with our teen librarian to bring your idea to life. Each machine and other materials have limitations and time requirements. Please see below for more information. Pre-registration is recommended to reserve your spot. If not all claimed registration spots have arrived by 4:30PM, they will be given to those waiting. All services are provided for free to middle and high school (6-12 grade) students. Younger people and adults are not permitted in the area unless required to assist with a disability. Pre-registration will start 1 week before the start of the program. Please un-register yourself if you find you're unable to attend at a later date. Registration closes 1 hour before the start of the program. There will not be a waitlist for pre-registration. Drop-ins will be accepted if not all registration slots are filled and if not all registered individuals arrive by 4:30PM. The area is wheelchair accessible from the Children’s Room elevator. Other accommodations can be made available with request. ADA Accommodation Requests Please note that each device requires time to set up, use, and complete whatever task you're wanting to use the space for. Be sure that you have enough time in your schedule to attend the program. Not all tasks may be completed before the end of the program and you may need to return to get your completed items or pause your task and restart at another studio session. We appreciate your patience and flexibility. 3D Printing: All requested prints must take less than 4.5 hours to print. All requested prints will need to be picked up at a later date. Contact information is required for notification of pick-up. 3D print quality and time needed to complete prints is not guaranteed. Multiple objects can be printed as long as the total time does not exceed 4.5 hours. Poster Printing: All prints must be assembled on a 2”x3” canvas and printed as a.png. Please see the regularly scheduled poster printing event for further details. One poster per teen per day. GlowForge: Create a custom engraved object. Object should follow similar guidelines to the Custom Keychain Program. Complexity of request is at the discretion of the librarian. Sewing & Serger Machines: It is recommended that you bring your own fabric and thread if fabric is special or color is a factor. There are scrap material and thread available but we cannot guarantee material quality or availability. An iron and ironing board is also available Cricut: Basic Cricut supplies are available, such as construction and cardstock paper. If your project is specialized, such as requiring iron-on, you’ll need to bring your own materials. It is recommended that you know the requirements for any materials you provide. Button Press: TeenHQ offers two sizes of button presses. We cannot offer printing. If your bring your own printout of buttons, it must be printed on standard printer paper. Paper thicker than standard printer paper cannot be used on the button presses. All measurements below are diameter length in inches. Small Button Press: 1.25” Large Button Press: 2.25” Picture Size: 1.156” Cut Line: 1.629” Picture Size: 2.063” Cut Line: 2.625”

title: The Songs of Nature: An Art Exhibit
description: Since then, we started watercolor painting together on Thursdays.
parentSummary: Since then, we started watercolor painting together on Thursdays.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Lisha and Helen's exhibit will be on display in the lobby during Saratoga Library's open hours from Monday August 31 to October 30, 2026. About the Exhibit Lisha and Helen like to explore nature and often join the Los Gatos Art Association morning group to paint in oil. On Thursday mornings they join the Santa Clara Valley Watercolor Society to practice watercolor painting. They love nature and appreciate its beauty. Here are some glimpses of their observations of the natural beauty surrounding us. They hope you like their paintings. Helen Chen's Artist Statement My name is Helen Chen. Ever since I was a little girl, I liked to draw. I remembered after each class, I doodle on my books and notebooks. This habit lasted long into my school years and later in life. But at that time in China, there weren't any art classes I could take like the ones here in the United States. In addition, my parents didn't like the idea of me pursuing art. They were more concerned about me finding a good job for security and a good life. To them, this meant that I should become an engineer in the field of mathematics, physics or chemistry. They believed “学好数理化,走遍天下都不怕” or “Master math, physics, or chemistry, and you can go anywhere in the world without fear.” I took their practical advice and became an engineer. After working for a couple years in China, I came to America to pursue higher education. After I graduated and worked here for a few years, I discovered that the University Art store in San Jose offered oil painting classes. I joined the weekend oil painting workshop. However, because I didn't have any previous training, I found it extremely challenging and practiced intermittently. In 2012, I decided to take a watercolor and oil painting class at West Valley College. While I studied there, I met a lot of wonderful people and we became good friends. One of them introduced me to the Santa Clara Valley Watercolor Society (SCVWS). Since then, we started watercolor painting together on Thursdays. Through SCVWS I met a lot of kind and talented artists, and I am inspired by them. In addition, I go to the Los Gatos Art Association (LGAA) for oil painting. I also started learning from famous artists like Charles Reid, Ching Chung-Wei, and Richard Schmid by reading their books with a group of friends. Now, I mostly painted for fun and love to paint nature. I know I will have a long way to go to become a good artist, but I will keep going. Lisha's Artist Statement Since 2013, Lisha Wang has been an active member of plein air painting groups, the Santa Clara Watercolor Society and the Los Gatos art community. She loves to explore a variety of subjects and enjoys painting outdoors. Nature is her greatest inspiration, from blue skies, floating clouds, distant mountains and vast landscapes to small houses and barns in a field. She also loves painting people by capturing their emotions, posture and movements. These subjects have remained her favorite throughout the years. Lisha’s passion for painting began with the childhood activity of chalk drawing on concrete floors. She developed her painting skills by attending various art classes and live demonstrations of water color and oil painting, as while as participating in artist conferences. For more than 15 years, Lisha has enjoyed PleinAir painting with fellow artists. These experiences and practices have deepened her understanding of artistic expression as seen by human eyes. Lisha believes that painting is more than simply creating beautiful images. It is about observing the world with gratitude, and sharing moments of beauty with others by using brushes and colors.

title: CNPS: talk #2  Transforming HOA Landscapes with Native Plants & AB 1572
description: Speaker Bio: Shelkie is a landscape designer and founder of WaterEfficientGardens.com, an online landscape design business specializing in low-water and California native garden designs.
parentSummary: Speaker Bio: Shelkie is a landscape designer and founder of WaterEfficientGardens.com, an online landscape design business specializing in low-water and California native garden designs.
sourceDescriptionRaw: HOA Parking Strip landscaped with California Native Plants As California advances its water conservation goals, traditional HOA turf policies are undergoing a major shift. Starting January 1, 2029, Assembly Bill 1572 will prohibit the use of potable water for non-functional turf in HOA common areas - a mandate that will be strictly enforced. For homeowners and board members, this regulatory shift presents a powerful opportunity to replace lawn areas with native landscaping that conserves water and restores local biodiversity. In this presentation, Shelkie Tao will share why converting lawns to California native plants yields far greater long-term benefits than standard low-water alternatives. She will cover practical strategies for balancing ecological performance with polished visual appeal, selecting climate-appropriate species that thrive in structured garden settings, and effectively communicating design intent to HOA boards. Attendees will leave with actionable steps for replacing thirsty turf with vibrant, ecosystem-friendly landscapes that satisfy state mandates while enhancing neighborhood character. Speaker Bio: Shelkie is a landscape designer and founder of WaterEfficientGardens.com, an online landscape design business specializing in low-water and California native garden designs. As a sustainability-driven entrepreneur, she is committed to developing attractive, water-efficient, and ecosystem-friendly landscaping solutions. Her design work has been featured by the statewide Save Our Water campaign. Prior to founding Water Efficient Gardens, Shelkie worked for over a decade in the Silicon Valley high-tech industry. She earned a Certificate of Achievement in Environmental Horticulture and Design from Foothill College, holds an MBA from the UCLA Anderson School of Management, and is an avid trail runner who has completed 21 marathons. title: Why Are Exoplanetary Systems Unlike the Solar System?
description: In this talk, we will explore the expectations of planet formation theory, and the constraints that are now available form observations, as we work toward the goal of understanding how common Earth-like worlds are and finding such cosmic neighbors.
parentSummary: In this talk, we will explore the expectations of planet formation theory, and the constraints that are now available form observations, as we work toward the goal of understanding how common Earth-like worlds are and finding such cosmic neighbors.
sourceDescriptionRaw: NASA's Kepler mission discovered over 4,400 transiting planets around other stars, including over 700 systems with multiple planets. This sample of exoplanet systems enables us to study planetary systems as a population, and test planet formation theory. The results are that our Solar System has a relatively rare configuration, and we don't know why. In this talk, we will explore the expectations of planet formation theory, and the constraints that are now available form observations, as we work toward the goal of understanding how common Earth-like worlds are and finding such cosmic neighbors. Speaker Daniel Jontof-Hutter is an associate professor of physics and astronomy at the University of the Pacific in Stockton. He studies planetary dynamics, what we can learn about planetary systems from their motion. His research goals include pushing the characterization of low-mass exoplanets toward the terrestrial regime, using big data and dynamical simulations. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

title: Night Sky Journey
description: Finally, you’ll leave the Solar System and explore the stars and nebulae of our home galaxy, the Milky Way.
parentSummary: Finally, you’ll leave the Solar System and explore the stars and nebulae of our home galaxy, the Milky Way.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Join Docent Naturalists Liza Coe, Catherine Xun, Dave Kocsis, Naureen Moon, NASA scientists, and local amateur astronomers for an evening observing the night sky. Neptune and Saturn will be visible (weather permitting). You'll begin with a close-up look at rocks from the Moon, Mars, and across the Solar System. Gaze through telescopes for detailed views of the lunar surface, continue the journey farther to Saturn’s spectacular rings and moons, and then go beyond to blue Neptune. Finally, you’ll leave the Solar System and explore the stars and nebulae of our home galaxy, the Milky Way. (Note: This activity is not a hike but will be held in the Skyline Circle Parking Area, a short walk from where you’ll park your cars.) Bring layered clothing to stay warm. Reservations are required and will be accepted on or after October 3 at 12:00 p.m. (Noon) and close October 16 at 2:00 p.m.

title: Forgotten Voices: Italian Americans Uprooted in Wartime California
description: Learn about surveillance, civil rights violations, and the long-buried trauma passed through generations.
parentSummary: Learn about surveillance, civil rights violations, and the long-buried trauma passed through generations.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Dive into a lesser-known chapter of American history: the experiences of Italian Americans on the West Coast during World War II. Through archival photos, historical context, and personal storytelling, Lindsay examines the impact of Executive Order 9066 on Italian American communities, especially in the Bay Area. Learn about surveillance, civil rights violations, and the long-buried trauma passed through generations. Highlights include: The little-known internment of Italian Americans alongside Japanese and German communities The devastation of family-run industries like fishing in California Stories of resilience, cultural erasure, and rediscovery Legislation and resolutions acknowledging past injustices Lindsay Marie Morris is a novelist and journalist based in Los Angeles. Her novels are inspired by her Sicilian-American roots and are grounded in years of historical research, from family archives and oral history interviews to wartime records and on-the-ground exploration in her novel settings. All are welcome. No registration needed. This program celebrates Italian-American Heritage and Culture Month. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

title: Forgotten Voices: Italian Americans Uprooted in Wartime California
description: Learn about surveillance, civil rights violations, and the long-buried trauma passed through generations.
parentSummary: Learn about surveillance, civil rights violations, and the long-buried trauma passed through generations.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Dive into a lesser-known chapter of American history: the experiences of Italian Americans on the West Coast during World War II. Through archival photos, historical context, and personal storytelling, Lindsay examines the impact of Executive Order 9066 on Italian American communities, especially in the Bay Area. Learn about surveillance, civil rights violations, and the long-buried trauma passed through generations. Highlights include: -The little-known internment of Italian Americans alongside Japanese and German communities -The devastation of family-run industries like fishing in California -Stories of resilience, cultural erasure, and rediscovery -Legislation and resolutions acknowledging past injustices Lindsay Marie Morris is a novelist and journalist based in Los Angeles. Her novels are inspired by her Sicilian-American roots and are grounded in years of historical research, from family archives and oral history interviews to wartime records and on-the-ground exploration in her novel settings. All are welcome. No registration needed. This program celebrates Italian-American Heritage and Culture Month. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. title: Family Fun with Flowers
description: This is a morning of making something beautiful together, side by side at the same table.
parentSummary: This is a morning of making something beautiful together, side by side at the same table.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Bring the whole family for a hands-on flower arranging class, whether you’re an adult or a child. This is a morning of making something beautiful together, side by side at the same table. You’ll work in adult-and-child pairs, with all the containers, flowers, and materials provided. Our instructor will guide you step by step, so there’s nothing to prepare and no experience needed. By the end, each pair will have created two arrangements to take home, one to keep and one to give. Along the way you’ll pick up the simple techniques that make flowers look their best, the kind you can use again at your own kitchen table. Mostly, though, it’s about the pleasure of arranging flowers with someone you love, in the middle of the garden on a Saturday morning. No experience is needed. Just bring your curiosity, and gloves and clippers if you have them. Required Materials If you have them, please bring gloves, clippers (adult), and scissors (child). Instructor Bio Karen Flores earned her certificate in traditional floral design at Filoli. She spent over ten years there teaching family flower arranging classes. She currently teaches for local garden clubs, rose societies and the Pink Ribbon Good groups. Karen is an accredited Floral Design judge for the Garden Club of America and for the American Rose Society. She enjoys sharing her love of flowers with the younger generation. title: Giving Thanks
description: Give thanks to Native Californians by exploring how they cared for the land since time immemorial before the arrival of settler-colonialists.
parentSummary: Give thanks to Native Californians by exploring how they cared for the land since time immemorial before the arrival of settler-colonialists.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Give thanks to Native Californians by exploring how they cared for the land since time immemorial before the arrival of settler-colonialists. Join Docent Naturalists Marie Faust Evitt, Nancy Weintraub, and Megan Elmore for a moderately-paced hike along the beautiful Ipiwa, Alpine Loop, and Sunny Jim trails. You’ll observe grassland, chaparral, and riparian habitats while discovering how local Native tribes use strategies such as cultural burning and regular pruning to nurture plants and ensure abundant food and materials for homes, baskets, and medicine. Children who can comfortably hike more than four miles are welcome. Bring a snack for a break at Alpine Pond.

title: Tidal Marsh Appreciation
description: Join Docent Naturalists Susan Bernhard, Ann Reisenauer, and Alison Hurst to explore the flora, fauna, and environmental issues of the salt marshes on this leisurely-paced, family-friendly walk along the Bay Trail.
parentSummary: Join Docent Naturalists Susan Bernhard, Ann Reisenauer, and Alison Hurst to explore the flora, fauna, and environmental issues of the salt marshes on this leisurely-paced, family-friendly walk along the Bay Trail.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Tidal salt marshes flood twice each day. They provide critical habitat for marine invertebrates such as oysters, mussels, and clams, shorebirds, and specialized native plants like pickleweed. Additionally, the baylands are on the Pacific Flyway, the great bird migration route between Alaska and South America. But wetlands are easy to overlook, often underappreciated, and threatened by climate change. Join Docent Naturalists Susan Bernhard, Ann Reisenauer, and Alison Hurst to explore the flora, fauna, and environmental issues of the salt marshes on this leisurely-paced, family-friendly walk along the Bay Trail.

title: Hip Hop Nutcracker - Broadway San Jose
description: Just like the original, in The Hip Hop Nutcracker, Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince go on a dream adventure battling a gang of mice, visiting the land of sweets and learning the lessons of the holiday season.
parentSummary: Just like the original, in The Hip Hop Nutcracker, Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince go on a dream adventure battling a gang of mice, visiting the land of sweets and learning the lessons of the holiday season.
sourceDescriptionRaw: | Performances: December 2-3, 2026 | A holiday mash-up for the whole family, The Hip Hop Nutcracker returns for another spectacular tour. Directed and choreographed by Tony and Olivier Award-nominated Jennifer Weber, this contemporary dance spectacle is a re-mixed and re-imagined version of the classic, smashing hip hop dance and Tchaikovsky’s timeless music together into a heart-stirring and inspirational holiday event. The Hip Hop Nutcracker is brought to life by a powerhouse cast of a dozen all-star dancers, a DJ, a violinist, and MC Kurtis Blow, one of hip hop’s founding fathers, who opens the show with a short set. Just like the original, in The Hip Hop Nutcracker, Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince go on a dream adventure battling a gang of mice, visiting the land of sweets and learning the lessons of the holiday season. Innovative digital graffiti and visuals transform the landscape of E.T.A. Hoffmann’s beloved story from traditional 19th Century Germany to the vibrant, diverse sights and sounds of contemporary New York City. Grab your family and friends and let the dynamic performers of The Hip Hop Nutcracker take you on a journey that celebrates love, community and the magic of the holiday season. Performances: ● Wed., December 2, 2026 @ 7:00pm ● Thur., December 3, 2026 @ 7:00pm > CPA Events Calendar > Visitor FAQs

title: My Very First Symphony
description: Our instrument petting zoo lets little hands explore real orchestral instruments up close.
parentSummary: Our instrument petting zoo lets little hands explore real orchestral instruments up close.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Sunday, March 7, 2027 at 11 a.m. California Theatre, San Jose, CA Concert Length Approx. 55 minutes No intermission $25 - Child $40 - Adult Monique Hafen Adams, narrator Symphony San Jose The Young Person’s Guide to the Orchestra My Very First Symphony is a special one-hour concert presented by Symphony San Jose featuring Britten’s The Young Person’s Guide to the Orchestra, ideal for families with toddlers, preschoolers, and young children. Brilliantly inventive and endlessly engaging, Britten’s The Young Person’s Guide to the Orchestra takes listeners on a tour of the ensemble, revealing how the personality of each instrument and their respective families contribute to the symphonic sound. Introducing children to classical music opens a world of imagination, emotion, and discovery. Live orchestral performances captivate young minds with vibrant sounds, dynamic storytelling, and the magic of musicians creating music together in real time. These early experiences spark curiosity, build listening skills, and create lasting memories that can inspire a lifelong love of music and the arts. Children aged one year and older require a ticket for entry. No furry friends here—just something even better! Our instrument petting zoo lets little hands explore real orchestral instruments up close. Kids can touch a violin, tap on percussion, and discover the sounds that bring music to life. It’s a fun, interactive way to turn curious toddlers into engaged listeners before the concert even starts. Join us one hour prior to the concert and let the musical adventure begin! Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday: 12 p.m. – 4 p.m. Monday – Friday, 10am-5pm

title: Disney's Dare to Dream Jr.
description: As the trainees work together to discover their own dreams, they uncover the power that imagination and teamwork have to make anything possible.
parentSummary: As the trainees work together to discover their own dreams, they uncover the power that imagination and teamwork have to make anything possible.
sourceDescriptionRaw: | Performances: June 23-27 | Children's Musical Theater San Jose (CMT San Jose) presents Disney's Dare to Dream JR., a musical revue that follows an eager group of trainees on their first day at a fictional Walt Disney Imagineering Studio. As the trainees work together to discover their own dreams, they uncover the power that imagination and teamwork have to make anything possible. Celebrating 100 years of Disney music, the production features 20 songs spanning a century of beloved films, including selections making their stage debut alongside favorites from The Princess and the Frog, Coco, Encanto, and Frozen II. Now in its 59th season, CMT San Jose is one of the region's premier youth performing arts organizations, offering training and performance opportunities to thousands of young artists each year. CMT San Jose trains and educates today's youth through musical theater to set and achieve high artistic and personal goals, and to inspire them to become exemplary artists, patrons and citizens of tomorrow. The organization is dedicated to fostering creativity and a lifelong love of the performing arts in a supportive and inclusive environment.
